records.decision: The Welsh Government plans to adopt a centralised system for childcare funding similar to HM Revenue and Customs by 2020.

evidence.quote: yesterday, when we made the statement following the announcement of the introduction of the Childcare Funding (Wales) Bill, we made clear that our preferred option, as put within that framework Bill, is actually to build on, and to learn from the lessons as well, the model of the HM Revenue and Customs type of model, where you actually have—and this, by the way, is supported by local authority providers out there—one system that is a centralised system, where there is clarity, that is handled, that has elements of information sharing between Government departments, such as the Department for Work and Pensions, and so on, so that the work is done for the parents, and the work is done for the local authorities; much cleaner, much simpler.

evidence.quote: How confident are you that you can achieve that by 2020?

records.decision: The preferred option for the childcare funding system is to build on and learn from the model of the HM Revenue and Customs type of model, where there is a centralised system.

records.decision: It was discussed that parents should be made aware of the UK tax-free childcare offer.
rationale: To avoid confusion and ensure parents access the best offer for them.
conditions: The pilots will provide more learning.

evidence.quote: I wonder, Minister, whether what you're doing, in a very good way, to promote your project—people will see that as the childcare offer and, at least in my experience, very few parents are aware of the tax-free childcare on a UK basis.
evidence.speaker: Mark Reckless AM

evidence.quote: You're right—sorry. That's absolutely one of the lessons we've learnt from even this early stage of the early implementers, because there are elements of a childcare offer within the tax offer, within universal credit, within working tax credit. There are little bits of different ones and it does cause confusion.
evidence.speaker: Huw Irranca-Davies AM

evidence.quote: So, as you go into the Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs criteria—you have a £100,000 cap, as well as the £6,000 minimum wage cap, and you're getting HMRC to say whether people are eligible, which requires them to set up that account with HMRC—will you assure this committee that you will make sure that parents who are doing that are aware of the UK tax-free childcare offer, and that their providers also are?
evidence.speaker: Mark Reckless AM

evidence.quote: Yes, absolutely. And I think, if it's okay, Owain would like to add something as well.
evidence.speaker: Huw Irranca-Davies AM
